newsitem.title: FRANCE: French far-right mayor in row over Jewish writer.
newsitem.headline: French far-right mayor in row over Jewish writer.

text.p: The far-right mayor of the French Mediterranean port of Toulon is locked in a fresh row with intellectuals and artists after he objected to a tribute planned for Jewish writer Marek Halter.

Mayor Jean-Marie Le Chevallier has said the tribute, planned during next month's local book fair, was "inopportune" because Halter, a Polish-born survivor of the World War Two Warsaw ghetto, supported immigration in France.
"I grieve," Halter said at the weekend. "It is the first time since I arrived in France aged 14...that I feel racism against myself."

Le Chevallier said he would prefer to celebrate Brigitte Bardot, the former film star turned animal rights defender who recently came under fire for an attack on Arab immigrants and praising Jean-Marie Le Pen, the leader of Le Chevallier's National Front.
Le Pen, who advocates sending immigrants home and giving preference to French nationals for everything from jobs to housing, won 15 percent of the vote in last year's presidential election.
Several writers have come out in support of Halter who said he would visit Toulon anyway for the November 22-24 book fair.

Culture Minister Philippe Douste-Blazy proposed to take over the fair from local authorities so that the tribute to Halter could go ahead, and a group of Toulon residents proposed to hand the writer a symbolic prize.
Halter is best known for his best-seller "Abraham's Memoirs" recounting the wandering of a Jewish family over the centuries.
Toulon was the biggest of three towns captured by the National Front last year in municipal elections which gave the far-right group control of its first towns.
Le Chevallier has had other brushes with artists this year.

He withdrew subsidies from a cultural centre where artists had gathered to protest against its policies, and was accused by politicians of censorship after a popular rap group was dropped from a Toulon music festival.

Another National Front mayor, in the southern town of Orange, has been accused in a government-commissioned report of banning books about racism or with a leftist or multi-cultural bent from the municipal library.
Mayor Jacques Bompard denied banning books and said he was trying to diversify the library.
